summary:
Çorum province stands under the national framework applicable across Türkiye. The sources assembled for this province record no Çorum-specific enforcement actions, incidents or institutions; the findings below are national, and they are what a visitor to Çorum would be subject to.

Human Rights Watch reported on 29 October 2025 that a leaked draft of Türkiye's 11th Judicial Package would amend penal-code article 225 to punish conduct "contrary to biological sex" with up to three years in prison, and would allow charges against anyone taking part in a same-sex engagement or marriage ceremony, carrying up to four years. Under civil-code article 40 the same draft would raise the minimum age for gender-affirming care from 18 to 25 and impose a permanent-infertility requirement, with providers facing fines and up to seven years and patients up to three years. Fifteen LGBT groups and the Turkish Medical Association objected, and Human Rights Watch called for withdrawal of the package. Whether the package has since passed is unresolved in the sources.
tangentialFactors:
The draft provisions sit within a broader pattern of state hostility recorded nationally: the Kaos GL LGBTI+ Human Rights Report 2025 counted 313 violations over the year, roughly two and a half times the 2024 total, dominated by 299 detention decisions. Turkish Minute's coverage of the same report counted six deaths linked to anti-LGBTQ violence in 2025, three classified as hate killings, with transgender individuals disproportionately affected.

Çorum's own record contains no comparable incident data, so the province's practical position cannot be distinguished from the national pattern on the sources available.
localsOnly: For LGBT residents of Çorum, the draft 11th Judicial Package would tighten penal-code article 225 and civil-code article 40 as described above, with gender-affirming care access narrowed to ages 25 and over and conditioned on permanent infertility. Türkiye has no comprehensive law prohibiting discrimination on sexual orientation or gender identity, and hormone replacement therapy is not covered by the government healthcare system.
outOfScopeNotes: Whether the 11th Judicial Package has been enacted since the 29 October 2025 report is unresolved in the sources. No Çorum-specific enforcement, incident or institutional data was identified; the province's position is carried entirely by the national framework.
